title: Design: Long and unusual names stay in their own rows in the Customer chip panel
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, a payer, with a long name with spaces that no other customer has, at least 60 characters (for example Northern Plains Heavy Truck and Trailer Repair Services West).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, a payer, whose name is customer A's name with every space taken out (for example NorthernPlainsHeavyTruckandTrailerRepairServicesWest).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer C, a payer, with a name that no other customer has and that includes each of the characters & " ' < > (for example A&B "Fleet" O'Neil <Parts> & Sons).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer D, the asset's owner.
  • If a name field stops before the end of a name, use the longest name it takes.
  • Have a new asset for this test, asset 1, owned by customer D, with three work orders for customer D at the test location, billed to customer A, customer B and customer C in turn, so the chip lists all four customers.
  • Open the attached picture bt-p7-03-after-customer-chip-open.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open asset 1's Work Orders tab from customer D's page.
  2. Click the "Customer" filter chip.
  3. Click the tick box in the row directly under customer B's row (if customer B's row is the last one, the row directly above it).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Three work orders are listed.

Step 2:

  • The panel lists customer A, customer B, customer C and customer D.
  • Customer A's name stays inside its own row: no part of it covers the row under it, and that row's text can be read.
  • Customer B's name stays inside its own row: no part of it covers the row under it, and that row's text can be read.
  • Customer C's name shows exactly as saved: the & " ' < > characters appear as typed, not changed into other characters or codes.
  • Every row's tick box is fully visible.

Step 3:

  • The customer in that row is ticked; customer B stays unticked.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12316 (Story 14, Asset Work Orders tab: whole history and Customer filter)

  • S14-R3: “Its options are every customer on the asset's work orders, as customer or Bill To, A to Z.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), version 1794510417-a68d (its boards are byte-identical to version 1794239066-4906 read 9 Nov 2026), read 13 Nov 2026: pictures "Customer chip open" (page 7 "Asset Work Orders tab", New, no before exists). Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bt-p7-03-after-customer-chip-open.png

The design's own words:

  • “"All customers" ticked, then "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow.", then each customer on the asset's work orders, as customer or Bill To, A to Z: "Kolosov's Diesel Repair", "Quartzsite Truck Service & Repair".”

The design draws this place with ordinary names only; it draws no long name without spaces and no name with & " ' < >. The stress check follows the design-case checklist (lesson L-21); the expected words come from the PRD quotes above.
